reported.title: Debounce timer never initialized, first press may be missed
reported.description: reqEdge starts at 0 and is only set when raw changes; if the button is already LOW at boot or the first transition happens before millis() reaches DEBOUNCE_MS, the (now - reqEdge) >= DEBOUNCE_MS check can pass immediately or the edge timestamp is stale, causing the first request to be accepted without 35 ms of stability. Initialize reqEdge = millis() in setup and only accept a stable LOW after a full debounce window from the actual edge.

reported.title: Unlock not guaranteed within 200 ms of door open
reported.description: The door-open check runs every loop so unlock is fast, but there is no explicit timing guarantee and the lock is re-engaged logic-free; more importantly the door-open branch calls setLock(false) unconditionally every loop, which is fine, but the real issue is the request path can re-lock in the same loop iteration after unlock if the button is still held, violating 'wait for a new request after unlock'.

reported.title: Re-engages while button held after unlock
reported.description: After the door opens and unlocks, if the request button is still held LOW (stableReq already LOW), the engage condition stableReq==LOW && doorClosed() && !locked can fire again once the door closes without a new press, because there is no edge/latch requirement — only a level check. Need to require a fresh HIGH->LOW transition after unlock.

judge_input.spec:
- Request button on D2 (pull-up); door-closed sense on D3 (pull-up, closed = LOW); lock solenoid on D9.
- Lock D9 engages (HIGH) when request D2 is pressed while door D3 is closed (LOW).
- Unlock (D9 LOW) when the door opens (D3 HIGH); unlock within 200 ms of door open.
- Debounce the request contact with 35 ms of stability before engaging.
- Print `vault lock=<0|1> engages=<n>` every 1000 ms.
- Do not re-engage while already locked; wait for a new request after unlock.
